72 is the measure of the two marked angles. The angle $y°$ sits beside one of them on line $m$, so it is the supplement.
This sets the two marked angles supplementary. They are alternate interior angles, so they are equal.

solution.key_idea: Alternate interior angles are equal; then $y°$ forms a linear pair with one of them.
solution.steps:
What does the question ask? The value of $y$.
Plan. Use the parallel lines to find $x$, then the straight line $m$ to find $y$.
$3x + 12 = 5x - 28$ (alternate interior angles are equal)
$40 = 2x$, so $x = 20$ (solve)
$5(20) - 28 = 72$ (each marked angle is 72°)
$y = 180 - 72 = 108$ (linear pair on line m)
Why not 72? That is the marked angle, not $y$.
solution.be_careful: Finding $x = 20$ is only the halfway point.
solution.another_way: $y°$ and the angle $(3x + 12)°$ are same-side interior angles, so $y + 3x + 12 = 180$ once $x = 20$ is known.

solution.another_way: The larger angle is $\frac{4}{5}$ of 180°, which is 144°, so the smaller is 36°.

Plan. Turn the ratio into angles, then take the supplement.
$2k + 3k + 7k = 180$ (angle sum)
$k = 15$ (solve)
Angles: 30°, 45°, 105° (multiply)
$180 - 30 = 150$ (exterior angle is supplementary to 30°)
Why not 30? That is the interior angle.

solution.be_careful: The exterior angle at the smallest vertex is the largest exterior angle.
solution.another_way: The exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles: $\frac{3 + 7}{12}(180) = 150$.
